name: Lomita City Council Special Meeting
minutes_text:
MINUTES OF THE
  LOMITA CITY COUNCIL
  SPECIAL MEETING
  MONDAY, FEBRUARY 28, 2022

PURSUANT TO EXECUTIVE ORDER N-08.21 ISSUED BY GOVERNOR NEWSOM AND
A8361, THE PUBLIC AND COUNCIL PARTICIPATED IN THIS MEETING IN PERSON AND VIA
ZOOM.

1. OPENING CEREMONIES
  a  Call Meeting to Order

  The special meeting of the Lomita City Council was called to order by Mayor Segawa at
  6:00 p.m. on Monday, February 28,2022.

  b. Council Member Waronek led the flag salute and Council Member Uphoff gave the
  invocation.

  c. Roll Call

  PRESENT: Council Members: U phoff, Waronek, Mayor Pro Tem Waite, and Mayor Segawa
  (present in Council Chambers)

  Council Member'. Gazeley (participated via Zoom)

  ABSENT: None

  STAFF PRESENT: Ci ty Attorney Rusin and City Manager Smoot (present in Council
  Chambers)

  Public Works Director Dillon, Community and Economic Development Director Kapovich,
  Administrative Services Director Kamada, Planning Manager Repp Loadsman, Management
  Analyst Hernandez, and City Clerk Gregory (participated via Zoom)

2. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Mayor Segawa announced the time for oral communications. There being no requests to
  speak, Mayor Segawa closed oral communications.

3. PRESENTATIONS
  Mayor Segawa presented certificates of recognition to Deputy Ricky W. Sherman, Deputy
  Reece Souza, and Deputy Tami Bouse upon their retirement from the Los Angeles County
  Sheriffs Department.

  Chris Cagle, Regional Affairs Manager of the South Bay Workforce lnvestment Board,
  presented the second quarter summary and outlined the Board's enhanced business services
  program.

4. CONSENTAGENDA
  RECOMMENDED ACTION: That Consent Calendar ltems 4 a-e be approved.

  City Attorney Rusin noted an error on the agenda and clarified that the consent agenda items
  were items 4a-e. Council Member Waronek made a motion, seconded by Council Member
  Uphoff to approve the Consent Agenda items 4a-e.

  MOTION CARRIED by the following vote:

  AYES: Council Members: Gazeley, Uphoff, Waronek, Mayor Pro Tem Waite, and
  Mayor Segawa
  NOES: None
  ABSENT: None

  Approved the following consent calendar items:

  a  Motion to Waive Full Reading of Ordinances and that They be Read in Title Only

  RECOMMENDED ACTION: Approve Motion

  b. Second Amendment to the Agreement with Willdan Financial Services for Park &
  Recreation and Sewer lmpact Fee Studies

  RECOMMENDED AGTION: Approve the Amendment and authorize the City Manager
  and City Clerk to execute the agreement.

  c. Warrants/Payroll Register
  RECOMMENDED ACTION: Approve and file Warrants/Payroll Register

  d. 5 Year Contract with Gruber and Lopez, Inc. for Citywide Audit Services
  RECOMMENDED AGTION: Approve the five (5) year contract with Gruber and Lopez,
  lnc. for citywide audit services and authorize the City Manager and City Clerk to execute
  the agreement.

  Resolution of lntention Regarding Potential Transition to District-Based Elections

  RECOMMENDED ACTION: Adopt Resolution 2022-08 directing a schedule be brought
  back to take actions related to district-based elections in accordance with Elections Code
  section 10010(a) and declaring its intention to adopt an ordinance pursuantto Government
  Code section 34886 to transition the election of its City Councilmembers from an allarge
  electoral system to a district-based system and finding the same exempt from the
  California Environmental Quality Act or provide further or alternative direction to City Staff.

  At this time, Council Members shared oral communications and meeting attendance reports.

  Mayor Pro Tem Waite reported on the following:
  .  February '16 - Los Angeles County Economic Development Corporation's Economic
  Forecast
  .  February 25  -
  Torrance-South Bay YMCA Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Annual
  Brotherhood Breakfasl

  Council Member Gazeley reported on the following:
  o  Recent forum with L.A. County Sheriff Alex Villanueva, sponsored by the South Bay
  Cities Council of Govemments

  Council Member Uphoff reported on the following:
  o  February 15 - L.A. Metro South Bay Study Stakeholder Meeting
  .  February 15 - California Contract Cities Association Board of Directors Meeting
  .  February 16 - forum with L.A. County Sheriff Alex Villanueva, sponsored by the South
  Bay Cities Council of Governments

  Council Member Waronek reported on the following:
  o  Recent press conference relative to a proposed ballot initiative requiring music and art
  teachers on every school campus
  .  February 15 - California Contract Cities Association Board of Directors Meeting
  o  February 19 - Grand opening of Castillo Engineering & Construction
  .  March 2-4  -California Contract Cities Association Legislative Tour; while in
  Sacramento he plans to attend a press conference at the Capitol Building regarding
  proposed bills relative to catalytic convertors theft and street racing
  o  -
  March 7 meeting with L.A. County Sheriff Alex Villanueva and Marcel Rodarte,
  Executive Director of the California Contract Cities Association
  o  March 10 - Lomita-Harbor City Kiwanis Club Lemonade Day kickoff; the event is July
  I and mentors are needed
  .  Encouraged Lomita business owners to apply for grants of up to $10,000 with City
  staff

  City Manager Smoot clarified that the open application period for those grants begins today
  and ends March 5,2022.

  Mayor Segawa had nothing to report.

  SCHEDULED ITEMS

  None scheduled.

  PUBLIC HEARINGS

5. DISCUSSION AND CONSIDERATION OF AN URGENCY ORDINANCE RELATING TO
  URBAN LOT SPLITS AND TWO-UNIT RESIDENTIAL DEVELOPMENTS tN SINGLE-
  FAMILY ZONES AS ALLOWED BY SENATE BILL 9

  RECOMMENDED ACTION: Conduct public hearing and after City Attorney reads the title,
  adopt Urgency Ordinance No- 832U (for a period of 45 days) relating to Urban Lot Splits and
  Two-Unit Residential Developments in Single-Family Residential Zones as allowed by the
  State of California Senate Bill 9.

  Planning Manager Repp-Loadsman presented the staff report as per the agenda material.

  Mayor Segawa opened the public hearing at 6:45 p.m. As there were no requests from the
  public to speak on this item, Mayor Segawa closed the public hearing at 6:45 p.m. and brought
  the item back to Council for further discussion or a motion.

  City Attorney Rusin read the title of the urgency ordinance to be adopted.

  Council Member Waronek made a motion, seconded by Council Member Gazeley to approve
  the recommended action.

  MOTION CARRIED by the following vote:

  AYES: Council Members: Gazeley, Uphoff, Waronek, Mayor Pro Tem Waite, and
  Mayor Segawa
  NOES: None
  ABSENT: None

  Adopted the following titled ordinance:

  URGENCY ORDINANCE NO. 832U . AN URGENCY ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL
  OF THE CITY OF LOMITA, CALIFORNIA, RELATING TO URBAN LOT SPLITS AND
  TWO-UNIT RESIDENTIAL DEVELOPMENTS IN SINGLE.FAMILY RESIDENTIAL ZONES
  AS ALLOWED BY THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA SENATE BILL 9

6, ADJOURNMENT
  There being no further business to discuss, Mayor Segawa adjourned the meeting, at
  6:46 p.m.
